data.name: Damasien
data.long_meaning: In Christian tradition, Damasien is derived from the Greek name Damaskos, meaning 'of Damascus'. Damascus was the city where Saint Paul was converted to Christianity by Ananias, and this name is often given to boys in honor of this significant event.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents the transformative power of faith and the strength of conviction in one's beliefs.

in_hebrew.name: דמסיין
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם דמסיין מקורו ביוונית ומתורגם לעברית כעמיקות השלום והנחמה מאלוהים. השם משויך לנושאים של רוגע ושלווה ברוחניות הנוצרית.

in_greek.name: Δαμασκηνός
in_greek.meaning: Δαμασκηνός, από το Δαμασκό, σημαίνει τὸ εἰρηνικόν
in_greek.long_meaning: Ὁ Δαμασκηνός, ἕνας ὅρος ποὺ συνδέεται μὲ τὴν πόλη Δαμασκός, συμβολίζει τὴν εἰρήνην καὶ τὴν ἀνάπαυσιν ἐν Χριστῷ.

in_latin.name: Damasien
in_latin.meaning: Damasien, qui significat profunditas quietis et consolationis a Deo
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Damasien, origine Graeco, significat profunditatem quietis et consolationis a Deo. In traditione Christiana, nomen hoc saepe cum serenitate et pace spirituali coniungitur.

data.cultural_impact: The name Damasien holds a rich cultural association with the history of Christianity and the city of Damascus, which is considered one of the oldest continually inhabited cities in the world. It serves as a reminder of Saint Paul's conversion, the spread of Christianity in the Middle East, and the enduring influence of this ancient faith on the region.

It serves as a reminder of the importance of spiritual growth and conversion, evoking images of Paul's profound encounter with the risen Christ in Damascus and the continuous journey towards holiness.
